applies_why: The text decides a head-to-head collision on Isaiah 7:14 in which each side presses the other's link with its own chain read together ([CR2]'s 8:8 and 9:6-7 against [DR3]'s 7:16 and 8:3-4), which is exactly the chain-against-chain collision K-C governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: The phrase 'the stating-verse test DG-61 retires': reading one, the judge's closing clause grounds UNDERDETERMINED in a single verse's failure to state the mechanism in its own words, applying the retired test at the judge's seat; reading two, the clause merely notes that the sign verse alone decides nothing while the verdict rests on a footing balance -- I weigh reading one, because that clause is the only evaluative reason the judge wrote and no footing comparison of the two chains appears anywhere in the text.
why: The judge grounded its UNDERDETERMINED verdict on the sign verse's own-word silence about the mechanism -- the very stating-verse test K-C retires -- instead of weighing the defender's chain footing (8:8, 9:6-7) against the challenger's chain footing (7:16, 8:3-4) as the rule requires.
